Subject: SLO aggregation methods + alerting hooks (Novatech RFP follow-up)

Jonas / Lauren,

Thanks for the call this morning — Novatech legal and procurement had a couple follow-ups for the SLO section of the RFP (attached). Two specific asks we want clarified before the next review:

1) Aggregation: how do you compute the monthly uptime percentage? Is it a rolling 30-day window, calendar-month aggregation, or weighted-sample across provable uptime samples? We need the exact algorithm to reference in our contract.

2) Alerts & hooks: can Redwood provide webhooks (or a PagerDuty integration) for customer-facing SLO breaches, and can we define a separate alerting threshold for our tenant? If an exception is granted temporarily, how does that show up in dashboards and audit logs?

Aaron (auditor) is CC'd — he may request sample data or a short example of the aggregation calculations.

Please reply with the brief technical description and any artifacts we can attach to our procurement packet.

Best,

Sr. Procurement Manager, Novatech

Subject: Re: SLO aggregation methods + alerting hooks (Novatech RFP follow-up)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Below is a short, procurement-friendly summary plus pointers to artifacts. Happy to jump on a 30 min call if you prefer.

1) Aggregation algorithm (contract language):
- Primary SLO: Monthly uptime percentage is calculated as 1 - (total failed_requests_tokens / total_observed_requests_tokens) over a contract monthly window. For clarity we record per-minute success/failure counts and compute the weighted average across the contract month (calendar month by default).
- Rolling vs calendar: We default to calendar-month aggregation for SLA billing and credits. For operational dashboards we offer a rolling 30-day view; both are available in the dashboard and in exported CSVs.
- Sample visibility: We store per-minute time series of error rate and latency percentiles for 13 months (default retention). You can request a sampled export for the procurement review (we can provide a 7-day example slice).

2) Alerting & hooks:
- Integrations: We support both webhook delivery (customer-provided endpoint) and native PagerDuty/Slack integrations. Webhooks can be configured at the tenant level and can carry a standardized JSON payload containing: timestamp, slo_id, observed_value, threshold, window, and a link to the dashboard snapshot.
- Custom thresholds: Yes, customers may request custom alert thresholds for operational alerts (not contractual SLOs). Contractual SLO breach notifications are emitted based on the contract-defined thresholds and aggregation windows only.
- Exceptions: Temporary exceptions (approved by Redwood legal/ops) are recorded in the audit log and flagged on the SLO dashboard as an "exception window" with start/end timestamps and the approver name. Exceptions do not retroactively change recorded time series; they are applied as metadata to affected windows for credit calculations.

Artifacts we can attach: redwood_slo_definitions_v1.pdf (formal measurement definitions), a CSV example of aggregation math (slo-aggregation-examples.csv), and a Grafana read-only invite.

Next steps:
- I can attach the two artifacts and provision a read-only Grafana view for your procurement/audit team.
- If Aaron wants the 7-day sample export, tell me the preferred time range and we'll ship it via secure link.

Jonas

We can make an exception to provide a 7-day raw sample export and a temporary increase to per-minute retention for Novatech's pre-contract audit. This will be timeboxed to the audit window and flagged in our system. To proceed we need a signed Data Access Addendum (I can send the link).

Also, for the webhook we recommend using a replay-safe endpoint (idempotency key recommended) and TLS1.2+ with a mutual-auth option for higher security. We'll include an example payload and a sample replay script with the Grafana invite.

Thanks — Lauren
